item.title: PM Wong pledges 'new and better' jobs as AI disrupts industries, transforms economy
item.description: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong pledged to create new jobs as AI disrupts industries. He said every worker will be protected. “We may not be able to protect every job. But we will protect every worker,” said Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

item.title: Japanese trailblazer Nishikori to retire at end of season
item.description: Japanese tennis player Nishikori will retire at the end of the season. Japanese trailblazer Nishikori to retire at end of season.

item.title: Condemnation and protests against Israel’s raid of Gaza aid flotilla
item.description: Israel's raid of a Gaza aid flotilla sparked international condemnation. Protests followed the interception of aid boats. Israel has provoked international condemnation for its interception of Gaza-bound aid boats in international waters.

item.title: Hegseth argues Iran ceasefire ‘pauses’ deadline for Congress’s approval
item.description: Hegseth argued that the Iran ceasefire pauses the deadline for Congress's approval. The ceasefire affects the approval timeline. Hegseth argues Iran ceasefire ‘pauses’ deadline for Congress’s approval The Washington Post.

item.title: Trump signs bill to end record shutdown over immigration enforcement
item.description: The US House voted to end the record shutdown, providing funding for most Department of Homeland Security agencies. The vote provides funding for most Department of Homeland Security agencies, except for two subagencies responsible for immigration enforcement.

item.title: AI disruption will 'open new doors' as NTUC expands training committees to help workers
item.description: NTUC secretary-general Ng Chee Meng announced plans to expand training committees to help workers adapt to AI disruption. The labour movement aims to spur "collective action" through a new tripartite council.

item.title: 'US Not At War With Iran': Team Trump's Big Claim As 60-Day Clock Stops Today
item.description: US House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that the US is not at war with Iran as a 60-day deadline passed. The comment comes amid heightened tensions between the two countries.

item.title: Trump escalates pressure on Nato allies, signals troop cuts in Italy, Spain over Iran
item.description: US President Trump signaled potential troop cuts in Italy and Spain over Iran. He questioned why the US shouldn't reduce its military presence in the two NATO ally countries. 'Why shouldn’t I?': Trump escalates pressure on Nato allies, signals troop cuts in Italy, Spain over Iran The Times of India.

item.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Signals Plan to Maintain Control Over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei announced plans to establish "new legal frameworks" for the Strait of Hormuz. He also stated that Iran would retain its nuclear capabilities. Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a statement that Iran would establish “new legal frameworks” for the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: US official says Iran war truce 'terminated' hostilities for war powers deadline
item.description: A US official stated that the Iran war truce has "terminated" hostilities for the war powers deadline. The comment comes as tensions between the US and Iran continue. US official says Iran war truce 'terminated' hostilities for war powers deadline Reuters.

item.title: Trump Floats New Plan Aimed At Creating Maritime Alliance To Reopen Strait Of Hormuz
item.description: US President Donald Trump proposed a maritime alliance to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route. The plan aims to counter Iran's influence in the region. US Israel Iran War Ceasefire News Highlights.

item.title: ONE Profit Plunges 92% as Geopolitics and Overcapacity Squeeze Earnings - gCaptain
item.description: Container shipping company ONE reported a 92% plunge in profits due to geopolitical tensions and overcapacity in the market. The decline is a result of increased competition and trade disruptions.

item.title: Trump lifts tariffs on UK whiskey to toast departing King Charles
item.description: US President Donald Trump lifted tariffs on UK whiskey to honor King Charles III. The move is a gesture of goodwill towards the UK during the transition of monarchs. Trump lifts tariffs on UK whiskey to toast departing King Charles.

item.title: Israel may have to 'act again' against Iran, Defence Minister Katz says
item.description: Israel's Defence Minister Katz said Israel may act against Iran again. Pakistan is mediating. Pakistan said that it was actively engaged with the U. S. and Iran to end the war in West Asia.

item.title: Trump Says Iran "Dying To Make A Deal", Refuses To Call It War
item.description: Trump claimed Iran killed 42,000 people in two months. He wants a deal with Iran. Trump claimed that "Iran killed 42,000" people over the last two months. Trump Says Iran "Dying To Make A Deal", Refuses To Call It War.

item.title: Trump Says Lifting Scottish Whisky Tariffs To 'Honor' King Charles
item.description: US President Donald Trump removed tariffs on Scottish whisky in honor of King Charles III and Queen Camilla. The decision is a symbolic gesture of respect for the British royal family.

item.title: US gas reaches $4.30 per gallon; Trump says prices will drop after Iran war
item.description: US gas prices rose to $4.30 per gallon amid the Iran diplomatic deadlock. Price of petrol in US jumps by nearly 30 cents in one week amid Strait of Hormuz blockade and Iran diplomatic deadlock.

item.title: Palestinians mourn football loving teenager killed by Israeli army
item.description: Mourners in Hebron buried 16-year-old Ibrahim al-Khayatt shot by Israeli soldiers. Mourners in Hebron laid to rest 16-year-old Ibrahim al-Khayatt who was shot in the chest by Israeli soldiers. Palestinians mourn football loving teenager killed by Israeli army.

item.title: Hegseth testifies on Iran war before Senate committee: Key takeaways
item.description: The Pentagon chief testified on Iran war before a Senate committee for a second day. Pentagon chief testifies alongside top general for second day, in first public Congressional hearings since war began.
